technical_and_design_decisions: The development will be based on an existing Spring XD codebase (assumed to be provided and accessible). The new modules and changes will follow its established module and architecture patterns.
The Kafka integration will be implemented using Spring for Apache Kafka, leveraging its robust producer and consumer abstractions.
The `generator` source and `perf-meter` sink will be implemented as standard Spring XD modules, packaged as separate artifacts (jars).
The REST API for module deployment (U3) will leverage Spring's REST capabilities and will interact with the Spring XD admin server.
The sample application (U4) will be a standalone Spring Boot application that uses Spring XD's client libraries to deploy and interact with a stream.
The spike (U2) will focus on the low-level, non-high-level Kafka consumer API (the `KafkaConsumer` class) to understand its direct partition assignment and offset commit behavior.

Testing strategy will include unit tests for individual components and integration tests for modules, using a real or embedded Kafka broker where necessary (e.g., using Testcontainers or an embedded broker).
All development will assume access to a local development environment with the necessary Java (17+), Maven/Gradle, and Docker (for Kafka broker) tools.
assumptions: The core Spring XD framework and its admin server are stable and available as a dependency. No modifications to the core framework are required for this increment.
The `uber-jar` format for custom modules (U3) is already supported by the Spring XD build tooling.
The specification's 'databases (and others)' for U1 implies JDBC-compatible databases and at least HDFS. Implementation will cover these, with other sources being future work.
The effort estimates include design, coding, unit testing, and basic integration testing for each activity. They do not include long-running performance tuning cycles.
The 'simple consumer API' (U2) is interpreted as the low-level `org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.KafkaConsumer` API, not the high-level `KafkaMessageListenerContainer` abstraction.
The `perf-meter` sink (U6) will log metrics to the standard container log via SLF4J, as is conventional in Spring/XD applications.
The sample application (U4) is a reference project (GitHub repo) and does not require automated deployment into a production environment.

activities.activity_description: Set up the local development environment, clone/checkout the Spring XD codebase, ensure all dependencies are resolved, and verify the basic build and test cycle runs successfully.

activities.activity_name: Spike: Kafka Simple Consumer API Investigation (U2)
activities.activity_description: Research and document the functionality of the low-level Kafka Consumer API (`KafkaConsumer`). Create a proof-of-concept to demonstrate manual partition assignment and offset commit. Produce a technical document outlining findings, approach for integration, and next steps.

activities.activity_name: Implement Source Module for Bulk Ingestion from Databases/HDFS
activities.activity_description: Design and implement a new Spring XD source module that can read data from JDBC sources (databases) and HDFS. Include configurable properties for connection details, query/file path, etc. Implement error handling and batching for efficiency.

activities.activity_name: Implement REST API for Module Deployment (U3)
activities.activity_description: Develop a REST endpoint (likely within the existing admin server) that accepts a multipart file upload of an uber-jar, validates it, and deploys it as a custom module to the Spring XD runtime cluster.

activities.activity_name: Create Sample GitHub Project for Spring XD with Kafka
activities.activity_description: Create a new, standalone Maven/Gradle project. Code a sample application that uses Spring XD's client APIs to programmatically define and deploy a stream using Kafka as both the message bus and a source (e.g., a simple string-producing source). Include detailed README documentation.

Design and implement a Spring XD source module that generates synthetic messages. Implement configurable options: `numMsgs`, `msgSize`, `numThreads`. Ensure controlled message production rate for performance testing.

Design and implement a Spring XD sink module that acts as a performance meter. It should consume messages, maintain counters (total and rate), and log a formatted message (timestamp, count, rate) to the standard logger at specified intervals (e.g., every N messages).

activities.activity_name: Integration Test & Stream Configuration for Performance Measurement (U7)
activities.activity_description: Write the necessary Spring XD stream definitions and configuration to create the `generator | perf-meter` pipeline. Verify it runs end-to-end in the 'singlenode' container and correctly logs the performance metrics for a large message volume.

activities.activity_name: Write CI Test Coverage for Kafka Modules (U8)
activities.activity_description: Develop comprehensive test suites (unit and integration) for both the new/modified Kafka source module and the new Kafka sink module. Ensure tests cover core functionality, error conditions, and can be executed as part of the CI build pipeline.
Perform self-review of all code, write/update any necessary technical or user documentation, clean up any temporary spike code, and ensure all activities are integrated cleanly into the codebase.
